title: Design a file storage system like Google Drive or Dropbox.
description: Distributed file storage with upload, download, sharing, versioning, and CDN integration.

data.text: **Question:** Design a file storage system like Google Drive or Dropbox.

data.title: Functional Requirements
items: Upload and download files up to several gigabytes
File sharing with granular permissions (view, edit, admin)
Version history and rollback
Folder hierarchy and organization
Sync across multiple devices
Real-time collaboration and conflict resolution

data.title: Scale Assumptions
items: 100 million total users
1 billion total files stored
10 petabytes of total storage
1 million uploads per minute at peak
100 petabytes of monthly egress traffic
Average file size: 10 megabytes

data.text: Large files are split into chunks using a sliding window protocol. Each chunk is uploaded in parallel to multiple storage servers for redundancy. A metadata service tracks chunk locations and assembles the complete file on download. Clients resume interrupted uploads by retrying failed chunks.

data.title: Large File Handling
data.text: Uploading a 5GB file in one request risks timeouts and data loss. Always use chunked uploads with retry logic and checksums for integrity verification.

data.title: Backend and Tiering
items: Hot files: SSD-backed storage with low latency
Warm files: Standard object storage (S3, GCS)
Cold files: Archive storage with higher latency and lower cost
Erasure coding instead of full replication for cost savings
Deduplication to avoid storing identical chunks across users

data.title: CDN Integration
data.text: Serve frequently accessed files through a CDN with edge caching. Set short TTLs for mutable files and long TTLs for immutable assets like images and videos.

data.title: Horizontal and Global Scale
items: Distribute storage nodes across multiple regions for low latency
Use consistent hashing to map file IDs to storage nodes
Replicate chunks across failure domains for durability
Throttle egress per user to prevent abuse
Use a separate metadata database with read replicas

items.question: How do you handle concurrent edits to the same file?
items.answer: Use operational transformation or conflict-free replicated data types (CRDTs). Present conflicting versions to users for manual resolution.

items.question: How do you ensure data durability?
items.answer: Replicate each chunk across three or more failure domains. Use checksums on every chunk and periodically verify integrity with background scrubbers.

items.question: How do you handle versioning efficiently?
items.answer: Use copy-on-write semantics for efficient versioning. Store only the delta between versions and keep snapshots periodically for faster rollback.

items.question: How do you prevent unauthorized access?
items.answer: Use signed, time-limited URLs for downloads. Verify permissions at the metadata service before issuing any access token.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Chunked uploads with retry and checksums are essential for large files
Separate metadata from file data for independent scaling
Use CDN for low-latency downloads of popular files
Implement versioning with copy-on-write for efficiency
Multi-region storage provides low latency and disaster recovery
data.takeaway: File storage systems must balance latency, durability, and cost through tiered storage and chunk-based transfer protocols.
